Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
950 AM EDT Thu Aug 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Made a few minor changes to the aviation section to speak to 
the low clouds this morning, particularly over IAD. Also altered
the marine section slightly. Overall though, forecast remains on
track over the next several days. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Hot, humid conditions persist into next week, along with
  daily chances for shower and thunderstorms.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Hot, humid conditions persist into next week, 
along with daily chances for shower and thunderstorms.

The Bermuda High remains in place across the western Atlantic into 
next week. PWATS will be near or greater than 2" in the valleys with 
1-2" in the mountains. South to southwesterly flow is maintained 
over the Mid-Atlantic. Hot and humid conditions each afternoon, with 
highs reaching the upper 80s to low 90s, and heat indices in the low 
100s each of the Blue Ridge. 

A surface trough is progged to remain over the area through Friday. 
Aloft, pieces of shortwave energy continue passing overhead and help 
trigger scattered showers and thunderstorms each afternoon. Deep 
layer shear is forecast to increase through the weekend as the 
subtropical jet stream strengthens. Hotter conditions may cause 
relatively steeper low-level lapse rates and the wind field 
strengthens a bit (especially Friday). This is going to bring an 
increasing chance for strong to severe thunderstorms each day, with 
Friday and Saturday looking to have the highest chances. On 
Saturday, a more potent shortwave trough is forecast to move 
overhead that could aid in stronger, more organized severe 
convection. Damaging wind gusts will be the main threat.

A quasi-zonal flow aloft will develop Sunday into into next week. 
Sunday could bring a short reprieve as dry conditions prevail. 
Seasonably hot, humid conditions along with daily chances for 
showers and thunderstorms return Monday through most of next
week.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
MVFR to IFR CIGs remain over IAD for now, but are starting to
burn off. That being said, could see a SCT deck around 1000-1500
feet for a few more hours. Model guidance handled this cloud
deck poorly, but there is plenty of moisture around in the low- 
levels to keep a few clouds around this level for a while. 
Overall though, VFR conditions seem most likely in this period 
for the most part, with clouds around 3-4 kft. Elsewhere, VFR 
is expected. 

VFR conditions prevail for most of the time through early next 
week. South to southwest winds prevail for the foreseeable 
future as the Bermuda high persists across the western Atlantic.
Daily chances for showers and thunderstorms each afternoon and 
evening through early next week, which could result in periods 
of restrictions at affected terminals.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories could be needed for parts of the waters at 
times through Saturday, mainly in the late afternoon to evening.
Most days will be marginal, and likely handled by MWSs, but just
know it could get a bit breezy over the open waters each
afternoon. Otherwise, winds remain around 10 knots. Daily 
showers and thunderstorms expected each afternoon into next 
early week. Special Marine Warnings would accompany any of the 
stronger thunderstorms capable of producing frequent lightning 
and wind gusts over 35 knots.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Anomalies climb late this week in response to return southerly flow. 
Periods of coastal flooding are possible at times of high tide at 
sensitive locations.

&&
